**REST: simple, cache-friendly, but rigid.**
Single operation per endpoint → separate requests for related data (under-fetching), extra fields you don't need (over-fetching). HTTP caching works out-of-the-box; clients are straightforward to build. Cost: endpoint sprawl as product grows.

**GraphQL: query-shaped, exact fetch, but harder to cache.**
Client specifies fields → no over/under-fetching. Single endpoint → reduced surface area. Cost: POST requests bypass HTTP caching; server must prevent N+1 queries; teams need resolver discipline or face hidden performance cliffs.

**Pick REST if:** standard CRUD, cacheable content (static files, user profiles), small team, monitoring is simple. **Pick GraphQL if:** highly interconnected data (graph of users → posts → comments), mobile clients bandwidth-sensitive, complex queries common, you have infra expertise.

Hybrid approach (REST + caching layer) splits the difference but adds deployment complexity.
